question: 0.3.6: what did several conversations at once pay for in the sparse attention's decode, and what of it can go without changing a bit of the output?
machine: GMKtec EVO-X2 class, Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151), 128 GB, 96 GB carve; this session ran ~7% slower than 2026-09-29's (0.3.5 at 3K: 40.1 ms against 37.3 then)
model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, MTP off unless stated

in_graph_cost_by_repetition.method: STRIX_REPEAT=<op>:4 dispatches the op 4 more times inside the captured graph (each copy writes what the first wrote); the step's growth / 4 is the op's in-graph cost. 8 conversations of ~20K (multi_probe --n 8 --words 6000 --gen 128), 512K q8_0 pool
in_graph_cost_by_repetition.topk_radix_below_32_rows: +16.3 ms a step for 4 copies (101.8 -> 118.2 ms): ~340 us a strip
in_graph_cost_by_repetition.topk_row_kernel: +0.4 ms a step for 4 copies (97.6 -> 98.0 ms)
in_graph_cost_by_repetition.one_conversation_110K: the TOP_K of one row: no change either way (40.36 vs 40.37 ms a token); at ~210K 41.13 (radix) vs 41.19 (rows)

decode_score_kernel_in_server.method: STRIX_IDXD_BENCH=n: at the first strips of >= 8192 blocks with >= n queries, graphs off, after cudaDeviceSynchronize, both kernels 50 times each timed with events, scores compared bit for bit (identical every time)
decode_score_kernel_in_server.parts_of_v3_at_8x20K_rows_per_cell: without the key loads 41 us, with them ~214 us: the reads, not the dot products, -inf stores, query loads or slot masks

synthetic_row_strides.note: the same kernel reading rows k*i (256 B rows): one conversation (27392 blocks) / eight (40640 blocks)
synthetic_row_strides.not_the_cause: the KV pool size (256K pool: the same), concurrent copies (synchronized first: the same), the rows' region offsets (7 MiB apart: no effect once dense), padding rows (41 of 40640)
